attacks.scenario: Only Reviewer is explicitly compared with the Work Item claim. Implementer can author Hardener/QA reports using distinct producerId values, with no global invocation registry or Host-attestation verification specified.
attacks.expectedControl: Require every role producer identity to differ from Implementer and other roles; verify identities and invocation IDs against Host-issued attestations in an immutable candidate-bound registry.

attacks.scenario: Unique IDs can be regenerated or duplicated across retries or branches because uniqueness scope, persistence, and replay detection are unspecified.
attacks.expectedControl: Define uniqueness scope, persist an append-only invocation index, and reject duplicate IDs or reused attestations.

attacks.scenario: Source-access mode and a prepared manifest are claims; QA can receive source through symlinks, inherited cwd, Git metadata, environment, prompt text, or unrestricted runnable artifacts.
attacks.expectedControl: Build an isolated QA sandbox from an allowlisted manifest, reject symlinks, scrub environment and Git metadata, and verify delivered bundle digest.

attacks.scenario: Attack-surface extraction is unspecified and may be Implementer-authored or omit changed/transitive security surfaces.
attacks.expectedControl: Derive attack surfaces deterministically from frozen diff and protected-surface policy; require coverage or block on omissions.

attacks.scenario: A stable prompt ID can point to changed bytes after invocation unless registry snapshot and report bind to exact prompt bytes.
attacks.expectedControl: Bind prompt ID and digest to invocation manifest and reject registry revisions that differ.

attacks.scenario: Production, policy, or planning classification is not executable; changed verifier/schema/prompt dependencies may be misclassified as evidence-only.
attacks.expectedControl: Define canonical invalidation path map including schemas, verifier, policy, prompts, and transitive imports; test renames and deletions.

attacks.scenario: Unsupported claims can leave a Candidate unresolved indefinitely, while external maintainer reports lack an authenticated provenance format.
attacks.expectedControl: Specify external-attestation schema, issuer/key, expiry, and coverage; unsupported state remains non-passable until supplied.

attacks.scenario: Consolidation can drop blockers, rewrite severity, or mark findings repaired without links to originals.
attacks.expectedControl: Use append-only aggregation with immutable finding IDs, source invocation references, and completeness checks.

attacks.scenario: Minimum-floor mapping and transitive affected-surface detection are unspecified, allowing security changes to be classified low/quick.
attacks.expectedControl: Check in complete mapping and deterministic classifier; reject missing, conflicting, or downgraded classifications.

attacks.scenario: Failure normalization, thresholds, and escalation authority are undefined; cheap success may suppress escalation.
attacks.expectedControl: Define versioned normalization, thresholds, escalation schema, monotonic floor state, and tests.

attacks.scenario: A schema-valid postmortem can have empty derived fields under permissive 'where Evidence exists' wording.
attacks.expectedControl: Enumerate mandatory derivations and explicit unavailable reasons; bind fields to artifact digests.

attacks.scenario: No escaped defects or repeated work can be claimed when traces are missing or untrusted.
attacks.expectedControl: Use true/false/unknown facts with provenance; prohibit negative claims from incomplete histories.

attacks.scenario: Undefined cache keys permit reuse across prompts, policies, hosts, manifests, or ancestry.
attacks.expectedControl: Specify canonical key inputs including candidate/base, role, prompt, bundle, policy/schema/tool versions, and host attestation.

attacks.scenario: A repair can be labeled evidence-only to avoid rerunning semantic roles; production classification is not independently enforced.
attacks.expectedControl: Derive changed-file class from Git and policy; any non-evidence change invalidates all roles.

attacks.scenario: Resume can trust deleted, altered, or old-controller artifacts.
attacks.expectedControl: Content-address stage state and require artifact digest and version compatibility before resume.
